gaps.sentence: The ancient manuscript was written ___ papyrus.
gaps.explanation: Text is written ON a physical surface (on paper, on papyrus); 'in ink' for the substance.

gaps.sentence: He ___ the advice of his lawyer and stayed silent.
gaps.explanation: 'Follow advice' = act as advised; 'chase/run after' are literal pursuit.

gaps.sentence: She ___ a fortune by selling her flat at the right time.
gaps.explanation: 'Make a fortune / make money' is the collocation; 'gain' is not used with fortune this way.

gaps.sentence: I'd ___ you didn't mention this to anyone.
gaps.explanation: 'I would rather you didn't…' — would rather + subject + past form. 'Prefer' would need 'I'd prefer it if you didn't'.

gaps.sentence: Her first novel was an ___ success.
gaps.explanation: 'An overnight success' = sudden success; 'overdue' = later than expected.

gaps.sentence: The hotel ___ breakfast until eleven at weekends.
gaps.explanation: 'Serve breakfast' = provide it to guests; the other options don't take this pattern.

gaps.sentence: Don't forget to ___ off the oven when you finish.
gaps.explanation: 'Turn off' (or switch off) = stop a machine.

gaps.sentence: The jury took only two hours to reach a ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Reach a verdict' — the jury's formal decision; 'sentence' is the punishment given later.
